Segment AB slants through the whole solid, and point B is located at the far upper corner of the upper-right cube. Counting along the three mutually perpendicular directions of the cube edges, from A to B it crosses 3 units in the horizontal direction, crosses 2 units in the backward depth direction, and rises 2 units in the vertical direction. Reasoning: The edge length of each small cube is 1, so the three-dimensional coordinate displacement from A to B can be regarded as (3, 2, 2). By the three-dimensional distance formula, AB = sqrt(3^2 + 2^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(9 + 4 + 4) = sqrt(17).

method.method_draft: Use projections and two applications of the Pythagorean theorem. From the image, drop B straight down to the floor level at a point C. The vertical segment BC spans two cube heights, so BC = 2. The floor projection AC runs across the footprint of the cubes: it is the diagonal of a rectangle that is 3 unit cube-widths in one horizontal direction and 2 unit cube-depths in the other, so AC = sqrt(3^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(13). Since BC is perpendicular to the floor plane, triangle ACB is right, giving AB = sqrt(AC^2 + BC^2) = sqrt(13 + 4) = sqrt(17).
